A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GneissWeb research and provide complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C. Pagination and figure-formatting differences do not limit comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training comparisons and filtering ablations in Section 5 and Tables 1–7, plus scored document examples in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model-training comparisons, filtering ablations, and scored appendix examples.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.7 retain the same sharded substring deduplication, fastText classifiers, category-aware readability and extreme-tokenization filters, and ensemble decision rule.

E1.justification: The training-data sources and evaluation coverage are unchanged, including the 11 high-signal tasks and 20 extended tasks described in Appendix B.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched experiments. Table 1 corrects 'RefineWeb' to 'RefinedWeb', the name already used in Section 5.3; this is the same baseline with unchanged scores.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations, tokenizer, training budgets, sampling procedures, evaluation metrics, and zero-shot/few-shot settings remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendix B.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 retains the same deduplication, readability, extreme-tokenization, and ensemble-rule ablations. Appendix C's selected and rejected document examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three sampling-seed runs, means and standard deviations, plotted error bars, and coefficient-of-variation analysis. Figure 9 already contained error bars in v1.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and Appendix C retain their results. For example, Table 1 still reports high-signal scores of 58.40 ± 0.19 for GneissWeb and 56.26 ± 0.14 for FineWeb-V1.1.0. Figure 9 redisplays the same curves with revised axis presentation.

T1.justification: The TokensPerChar and TokensPerByte definitions, filtering inequalities, and ensemble logical expressions are unchanged. No theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same approximately 10-trillion-token dataset contribution, filtering innovations, quality–quantity tradeoff, and comparative-performance claims.

C2.justification: The filtering rationales and result interpretations are unchanged. Section 7 retains the limitations concerning restricted ablation searches, English-only testing, one tokenizer, and limited code and mathematics content.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware and training-time disclosures, data-processing information, code links, and statements about a future open-source release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 retains the same research positioning, and the bibliography contains the same 68 references. Reference pagination changes do not introduce or remove cited work.

P1.justification: v2 expands Santosh Borse's name, corrects Ravital to Revital Eres, updates the date, corrects the RefinedWeb label, and adds acknowledgments for four contributors. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 9 gains numerical y-axis tick labels and revised framing and proportions. Figure 1 moves from page 2 to page 3, with additional local text and reference reflow. All figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Adding the missing numerical y-axis labels makes Figure 9 easier to interpret quantitatively, while author-name and baseline-name corrections improve accuracy. These are limited presentation improvements; the scientific methods, evidence, claims, and limitations remain unchanged.
